litem.frameTop.hint:
----HINT----
1. After importing, click “Basic Analysis” manually.
2. First click on “Basic Analysis” will auto-open import window.
3. Do not disable ‘Render’ in Settings unless necessary. Disable 3D rendering for low-end systems.
4. Block IDs and replacement table can use either Chinese or game ID (e.g. 泥土 & minecraft:dirt)
5. Replacement format: oldBlock-newBlock, oldBlock2-newBlock2,...
	‘-’ separates old/new blocks, ‘,’ separates groups. You can mix Chinese and IDs.
	Add block properties after old block (for editing) or after new block (for output).
	All properties must be wrapped in braces {} and use key-value pairs like {"property":"value",...}. All strings must be in quotes!
Example: Furnace{"facing":"west"}-BlastFurnace{"facing":"east"}, OakSlab-OakSlab{"waterlogged":"false"}
Furnaces facing west → Blast furnaces facing east; All Oak slabs → non-waterlogged Oak slabs
litem.funcChange.6:
Pick from the list, or just type a block that isn't listed.
For block states write it like hopper{{"facing":"west"}}.
litem.funcNew.6: ID input can be pure English or Chinese name

LitematicaViewer V{} - What's new
1. Manual 3D Rendering now uses real textures: glass and other transparent blocks, signs and beds render correctly; click a block to see its state and container items
2. The 3D window adds all / range / single-layer view, step-by-step build splitting and entity hitboxes, and follows your theme colours
3. The web version is live at lite-viewer.com: view schematics, export materials, convert formats and replace blocks in your browser

web.thumb.title: Thumbnail
web.tip.fluid:
How many blocks of water, lava and other liquids the schematic has (u = blocks).
A big number means lots of flowing water or lava — mob farms, water elevators, item streams.
Bring buckets and mind the flow direction when placing them.
web.tip.redstone:
How “machine-like” the schematic is: the share of redstone parts and containers (hoppers, chests, furnaces…) among all blocks.
Higher = more of a farm or machine, lower = more of a building.
The single most-used block (usually the shell or filler) is left out first, so a big wall doesn’t drag the number down.

web.tut.convert: Convert format: hover it and pick .litematic / .nbt / .mcstructure / .schem / .schematic / .bp / .vschem, or “World save” — unzip the download into .minecraft/saves to walk around it in game. It saves what you see now, replacements included. “Game version” below saves a .litematic for 1.20.6+, 1.14–1.20.5 or 1.13 (same as the desktop “Convert to”).
web.tut.edit: Also: right-click the title to rename the structure and the description to edit it; click a container slot to put an item in; “Raw NBT” shows this block exactly as stored in the file; add a background (ocean, grass, End) at the bottom right.
web.tut.export: Export: hover “Export” to choose text, text by category, CSV, or CSV by category (CSV opens in Excel).
web.tut.gizmo: The axis widget at the top right (X red, Y green, Z blue) turns with the view; click an end to look from that side, or drag it to orbit. The small button below switches between perspective and orthographic (isometric).
web.tut.inspect: Inspect: left-click a block or an entity icon to see its name, ID and state; containers also list their items.
web.tut.kind: Hide / Highlight this kind: hidden blocks leave only a grey outer outline (can be turned off at the top right); highlighted blocks get one step brighter with a yellow outline, visible through walls. “Reset” at the top right. Also in the right-click menus.
web.tut.license: AGPL-3.0 licensed · third-party notices in NOTICE.md
web.tut.move: Move: W/S go forward/back along your view (look up to fly up), A/D strafe, Space/Shift straight up/down; adjust the speed at the bottom right.
web.tut.open: Open: drop a .litematic / .nbt / .mcstructure onto the page, or click “Open file”. Files stay in your browser and are never uploaded.
web.tut.replace: Replace blocks: left-click a block and open “Replace block / edit states” in its info panel. Pick what to change it to (similar blocks first), match by states and change states, choose all of that kind or just this one, then press Apply. Right-click “Quick replace” in the list or in 3D replaces as soon as you pick. Two-tall targets (doors, tall grass) ask what to do when the block above is taken; beds only swap with beds.
web.tut.title: How to use
web.tut.tools: Tools (right side, click a title to open): Replace blocks (several pairs at once, ⚙ for states), Thumbnail, Build steps and Contour map. For multi-region schematics, pick a region above the material list: 3D shows only that region and replacements only touch it.
web.tut.undo: After a replace you get an “Undo” button; “Restore original” goes back to the file as opened.
web.tut.url: Open from a link: paste a link to a schematic file on the start screen (GitHub, direct cloud links…), or drag a link in from another tab. The site has to allow web pages to read it; if not, download it first and drag it in.
web.tut.view: Look around: left-drag to rotate, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom. The slider at the bottom left shows layers.
